cities.intro: Get matched with architects licensed in California and fluent in Oakland's permit process — from seismic-retrofit additions to backyard ADUs. Entirely remote, escrow-backed, stamped and permit-ready.
cities.body1: Oakland sits in a high-seismic zone with its own Bureau of Building requirements, soft-story ordinances, and a design-review process that trips up out-of-area firms. Every architect we match is licensed in California and has cleared permits with the City of Oakland before.
cities.body2: That local fluency shows up where it counts: correctly detailed lateral systems, Title-24 energy compliance done right the first time, and drawing sets that plan-check reviewers recognize — so you spend less time in correction cycles and more time building.

states.intro: California is one of the most demanding permitting environments in the country — seismic requirements, wildfire overlays, coastal rules and Title-24 energy compliance all shape the drawing set. Here's what to expect, and how we match you to an architect licensed to stamp it.
states.body1: Every set submitted in California must be stamped by an architect licensed by the California Architects Board. Beyond licensure, the state layers requirements few other jurisdictions do: mandatory Title-24 energy compliance, seismic detailing tied to the local hazard zone, and — in much of the state — wildfire (WUI) ignition-resistant construction. These aren't optional line items; a set missing them is rejected at plan check.
states.body2: On top of state rules, each city and county adds its own review. Coastal jurisdictions trigger Coastal Commission steps, hillside lots require additional geotechnical and structural coordination, and historic districts add design review. Our jurisdiction database scores each of these so your estimate reflects the real complexity of your specific address, not a statewide average.
